title: Latency Pulseboard: per-model/route p50/p95/p99 with streaming vs blocking split
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Ship a reusable Grafana/Console Pulseboard that shows per-model and per-route latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) with an explicit decomposition for streaming vs blocking (non-streaming) IO paths, trace-link overlays for slow requests, and an actionable tail-latency investigation panel. This board should be compact for SRE/Platform on-call use, and also embeddable in runbooks and postmortems.

Motivation: Teams are currently blind to whether tail latency regressions are coming from streaming assembly (incremental token emission and network flush patterns) or blocking path e2e (full response compute). Existing dashboards mix modes and require multiple manual queries. This Pulseboard will provide one-click cohort drilling and trace hooks so engineers can go from a percentile spike to a correlated trace and request payload within 2 clicks.
acceptance_criteria: Pulseboard displays p50/p95/p99 time-series for selected model(s) and route(s)
Separate series (and stacked breakdown) for streaming vs blocking IO modes
Per-percentile sparklines with anomaly shading (configurable window) and SLO thresholds
Each percentile point supports drill-to-trace links that open the Trace Viewer with pre-populated trace_id/query
Tail-latency cohort table showing top 5 request shapes (by prompt length, model, route, streaming flag) with median and p99 and sample trace links
Panel with suggested mitigations (e.g., increase batching, enable prefix cache, fall back model variant) based on detected pattern
Dashboard can be filtered by time range, customer_tier, region, and model_variant
Automated dashboard provisioning via Terraform module and dashboard JSON schema in repo
Unit/Integration tests for telemetry queries validate that new metrics (e.g., servepath.stream_latency_ms) are present in prod metrics pipeline
tasks: Define metrics schema additions: servepath.streaming_latency_ms and servepath.blocking_latency_ms
Add trace hook: attach trace_id and request_shape tags to span root for quick-linking
Update metrics pipeline (OTel Collector + Vector) to ensure low-cardinality labels for route and model_version
Design Pulseboard layout and wireframes (console mock) and review with SRE/PM/Design
Implement Grafana panels and JSON export; add Terraform dashboard provisioning
Add automated regression test in telemetry CI that replays synthetic canary traffic and asserts p95 within expected range
Document dashboard usage and runbook steps in Confluence
Ship and monitor for 2 weeks; collect feedback and iterate

implementation_notes:
Metrics: Add two new histograms: servepath.streaming_latency_ms and servepath.blocking_latency_ms. Use OTLP histogram with explicit buckets to preserve percentile accuracy. In vector/otel-collector, add a reduce transform that collapses high-cardinality labels to model_family and route only for the dashboard feed.

Tracing: Instrument root span with attributes: service.route, model.version, request_shape=(prompt_tokens,completion_max_tokens), streaming=true|false. Implement a small HTTP endpoint in trace-viewer that accepts trace hints (trace_id, start_time) for fast lookup from the dashboard.

Query examples: In Grafana, p95 streaming: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(servepath_streaming_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_family, route)) . p99 similar but use 0.99 and 1m window for alerting.

Alerting: Create p95 > 1.5x baseline and p99 > 2x baseline alerts with annotations linking to Pulseboard. Baseline computed via rolling 28d median.

Deployment: Coordinate with infra to roll metric transform to prod in a canary region first. Dashboard Terraform module must be idempotent and accept a list of models/routes to pre-populate variables.
risks_and_mitigations: High-cardinality labels could blow up metrics cardinality - mitigation: add reduce transform and only publish model_family/model_variant as optional label
Streaming latency histograms may be sparse for low-traffic routes - mitigation: rely on synthetic canary traffic and fallback to aggregated family-level metrics
Trace linking may increase read load on trace storage - mitigation: enable rate-limited trace fetcher and cache recent traces in Redis for the Pulseboard
Dashboard proliferation - mitigation: create a single Pulseboard template and enforce provisioning via Terraform only
